topic: Unlocking Planar Graphs: Euler's Characteristic and Duality
target_audience: Undergraduate Computer Science or Mathematics students

sections.title: Prerequisites & Definitions
lecture_lines: A planar graph embeds without crossing edges.
The exterior region counts as a face.
animations: Display text 'A planar graph embeds without crossing edges.' in #FFFFFF.
Fade in a simple convex polyhedron in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Euler’s Characteristic Formula
lecture_lines: Euler's formula relates V, E, and F.
It states V minus E plus F equals 2.
This property holds for any connected planar graph.
Adding edges and vertices preserves this invariance.
The formula remains true for all complexity levels.
animations: Show 'V-E+F=2' remaining invariant as graph changes.
Highlight the whole formula in #FFFF00 for emphasis.
Verify result for a simple tetrahedron in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: The Concept of Duality
lecture_lines: A dual graph swaps faces and vertices.
Place a dual vertex in every face.
Connect dual vertices sharing an edge.
animations: Display original graph in #FFFFFF with vertices labeled.
Fade in dual points at the center of each face.
Connect dual points with lines in #FFFF00.

sections.title: Duality Properties
lecture_lines: This creates a perfect inverse symmetry.
A house graph transforms into its dual.
animations: Display duality table showing V=F and F=V in #FFFFFF.
Animate cube vertices merging into octahedron faces.
Overlay octahedron on cube to show symmetry in #FFFF00.
Highlight inverse vertex and face mapping in #00FF00.
Animate house graph transforming into its dual form.

sections.title: Application: Map Coloring & Complexity
lecture_lines: The Four Color Theorem is a consequence.
Maps become easy adjacency node problems.
animations: Display map of regions on a surface in #FFFFFF.
Represent regions as nodes in a graph using #0000FF.
Color graph nodes with four colors to demonstrate theorem.
